mcu_0160_080057e8.name: mcu_snapshot_copy_if_changed
mcu_0160_080057e8.summary: Copy a 7-word record to its shadow when the byte at +0x18 differs or a force flag is set
mcu_0160_080057e8.description: Compares the byte at offset 0x18 of the source record (param_1) with the same byte in the destination (param_2). If they differ, or the RAM force flag at 0x2000066D is non-zero, the seven 32-bit words at offsets 0x00..0x18 are copied from source to destination and the force flag is cleared. Otherwise nothing is written. It is a copy-on-change snapshot, so the destination mirrors the source after any change. The byte at +0x18 acts as the change indicator for the record.
mcu_0160_080057e8.notes: Owning subsystem not visible in this packet; only caller is mcu_0160_08004e78.

mcu_0160_08005e60.name: mcu_byte_sum_checksum16
mcu_0160_08005e60.summary: 16-bit byte-sum checksum over a buffer, returned as its bitwise complement
mcu_0160_08005e60.description: Adds the len unsigned bytes of the buffer into a 16-bit accumulator (the sum wraps modulo 65536) and returns the complement of that sum truncated to 16 bits. A zero-length buffer returns 0xFFFF. This is a simple additive checksum, not a CRC: summing the data together with the returned value gives 0xFFFF. Called from mcu_0160_08006460.

mcu_0160_08005e7c.description: When the request byte at 0x20001FC8 is set, the routine loads the countdown 0x20000644 with 0x567 (1383), clears the request and sets the active byte 0x2000066C. While active, each call decrements the countdown; once it is below 1 the active and request bytes are both cleared. The hold therefore lasts about 1383 calls of the caller's tick, plus one. mcu_0160_08005e7c.notes: The period of the calling tick is not visible here, so the real-time length is unknown. The purpose of the hold is a guess.

mcu_0160_080061a6.summary: Busy-wait until SysTick has counted down param_1 counts
mcu_0160_080061a6.description: Polls the SysTick current-value register (SYST_CVR, 0xE000E018) and accumulates the decrease between successive reads. When a read is larger than the previous one the counter has wrapped, so 0xFFFFFF is added, which assumes a 24-bit reload. The loop exits once the accumulated count reaches param_1, so the argument is in SysTick clock cycles, not microseconds. It runs at least one iteration even for a zero argument. Callers are mcu_0160_0800226c, mcu_0160_08007df4 and mcu_0160_0800d548.

mcu_0160_080062f0.name: mcu_fault_norm_sq_debounce_check
mcu_0160_080062f0.summary: Return 0 when the squared magnitude of (+0x18, +0x1C) exceeds the limit at +0x3C
mcu_0160_080062f0.description: Computes (x/8)^2 and (y/8)^2 for the s32 values x at +0x18 and y at +0x1C, shifts each product right by 15 and sums them, which is about (x^2 + y^2) / 2^21. If the sum is greater than the s32 limit at +0x3C, the counter 0x20000344 is incremented, and the function returns 0 only when the counter's previous value was above 3. Every other path clears the counter and returns 1. As written, the counter can only exceed 3 if another writer sets it, so the intended four-sample debounce does not accumulate by itself.

params.name: param_1
params.description: object with x (+0x18), y (+0x1C) and limit (+0x3C), all s32

returns.description: 1 = within limit or not tripped, 0 = tripped

mcu_0160_080062f0.notes: Check whether 0x20000344 is written anywhere else. The debounce logic looks incomplete or inverted.

mcu_0160_08006334.name: mcu_clarke_alpha_beta_step
mcu_0160_08006334.summary: Store the previous +0x20 sample at +0x18 and compute beta = (ia + 2*ib) / sqrt(3) in Q15
mcu_0160_08006334.description: Copies the sample at +0x20 into +0x18, a one-sample delay of the first component. It then computes beta = (value at +0x20 + 2 * value at +0x24) * 0x49E6 / 2^15 and writes it to +0x1C. The constant 0x49E6 / 2^15 = 0.5773 is 1/sqrt(3) in Q15. This matches the Clarke transform beta term for phase currents ia = +0x20 and ib = +0x24, though the field roles are inferred from the arithmetic. Always returns 1.

params.name: param_1
params.description: object with ia (+0x20), ib (+0x24), delayed alpha (+0x18), beta (+0x1C), s32

mcu_0160_0800635e.name: mcu_park_transform_deadband
mcu_0160_0800635e.summary: Park transform of (alpha, beta) with Q15 sin/cos at +0x34/+0x38 and a dead-band on d and q
mcu_0160_0800635e.description: Reads alpha at +0x18, beta at +0x1C, sin at +0x34 and cos at +0x38, all Q15. Computes d = alpha*cos + beta*sin into +0x10 and q = beta*cos - alpha*sin into +0x14, each product taken as a 64-bit value shifted right by 15. Any component whose absolute value is below the threshold param_2 is then forced to zero, which suppresses small values near zero. Called from mcu_0160_08007364.

params.name: param_1
params.description: object: alpha, beta, sin, cos in, d, q out

params.name: param_2
params.description: dead-band threshold, same units as d and q

mcu_0160_0800635e.notes: Park sign convention is the standard one; the field names are inferred.

mcu_0160_080063c0.name: mcu_inv_park_transform
mcu_0160_080063c0.summary: Inverse Park transform: (d, q) to (alpha, beta) using the Q15 sin/cos at +0x34/+0x38
mcu_0160_080063c0.description: Reads d from word 0 and q from word 1 of the int block, and sin from word 13 (+0x34) and cos from word 14 (+0x38), all Q15. Writes alpha = d*cos - q*sin to word 2 (+0x08) and beta = q*cos + d*sin to word 3 (+0x0C), each product shifted right by 15 after a 64-bit multiply. This is the inverse of mcu_park_transform_deadband. Called from mcu_0160_08007364. Always returns 1.

params.name: param_1
params.description: int block: d, q in; alpha, beta out; sin at +0x34, cos at +0x38

mcu_0160_08006580.name: mcu_f30_range_latch
mcu_0160_08006580.summary: Latch flag 0x2000010F from the magnitude of the s32 at 0x20000F30; argument 0 clears the latch

mcu_152_08006b58.name: mcu_tea_decrypt_block

mcu_0160_08006de8.name: mcu_limit_block_init_params

mcu_0160_08006de8.description: Writes param_8 to word 0, param_3 to word 2, param_4 to word 3, param_5 to word 4, param_6 to word 5, param_2 to word 6 and param_7 to word 7, and writes param_9 to the byte at +0x3C. mcu_0160_08006e18.name: mcu_limit_block_update
mcu_0160_08006e18.summary: Per-cycle limit update: bounds X and Y from two Q15 gains, output selected by mode bytes
mcu_0160_08006e18.description: Inputs are the block and four samples p2..p5. The block holds gains w0 and w1 (Q15), the current and previous sample (words 4 and 5), pointers to a reference S (word 6) and to the output (word 7), and mode bytes at +0x20 (enable), +0x21 (low clamp) and +0x22 (high clamp). It forms X = p3 + w0*(p4-p2) - w1*(p2-prev) and Y = p3 + w0*(p5-p2) - w1*(p2-prev), each product Q15 rounded, then selects the output: S when the enable byte is 0; max(S,Y) for the low clamp alone; min(S,X) for the high clamp alone; and with both, max(S,Y) if S <= X and X otherwise. A final rule forces a negative output to zero when the value at 0x20000F30 is <= 0 and bit 2 of 0x2000065D is clear. Intermediate values are copied to 0x20000350..0x200003A0 for monitoring.

returns.description: writes the output through the pointer in word 7

mcu_0160_08006e18.notes: The mode table and arithmetic are read directly from the code. The physical meaning of the gains, bounds and the 0x2000065D bit is unknown.

mcu_0160_08007078.name: mcu_lpf_q30_step_alt

This is an exponential moving average whose coefficient sets the time constant. The body is identical to mcu_lpf_q30_step (mcu_0160_0800721a), so the two are probably two copies of one helper in this build. Called from mcu_0160_08002e9c, mcu_0160_08007160 and mcu_12b_08003010.

mcu_0160_08007198.notes: Uses the same mode-byte convention as mcu_limit_block_update, but the +0x18 field is a byte here and a pointer there, so these may be different objects.

mcu_0160_08007ba4.name: mcu_tmr1_pwm_outputs_enable
mcu_0160_08007ba4.summary: Set TMR1 CH1-3 compare values to 0x1193 and enable channels 1-3 and their complementary outputs
mcu_0160_08007ba4.description: Writes 0x1193 (4499) to TMR1.C1DT, C2DT and C3DT (0x40012C34, 0x40012C38, 0x40012C3C), so all three PWM channels start at the same duty. The result is three-phase complementary PWM on the motor bridge. Dead-time is not set here. Called from mcu_0160_0800226c.
mcu_0160_08007ba4.notes: Register writes are certain. The bit names follow the usual timer layout and the duty period is not visible here.
